claims: "Where both spouses would otherwise be liable and one is in a Category 1 exemption category, a signed family agreement decides which of you claims the full exemption and which claims the half."
whys: The condition reads oddly. If only one spouse is in Category 1, the other has no exemption to split. The ATO family agreement (QC27036) seems to apply when both spouses qualify for an exemption and have dependants. Check the wording against the ATO page.

claims: Miscellaneous Award Level 1 is $978.10 a week ($25.74/hr). Fitness Industry Award Level 1 (line 613) is the same.
whys: This is below the 2026 award minimum of $1,004.90/wk ($26.44/hr) and below the 2026 National Minimum Wage after its 5.97% rise. It is also not a 4.75% uplift on the 2025 Level 1 rate if that rate equalled the 2025 NMW. Please confirm it against cl 15.1 of each consolidated award and Schedule A.1 of the Miscellaneous Award.

claims: Production and support staff ordinary hours can be worked Monday to Sunday between 7.00 am and midnight (cl 61.1(b)), so evenings and weekend daytime hours inside a normal week carry no loading. Saturday has no penalty rate.

whys: The penalty table for the same award (line 1001, cl 63.4) pays 200% (casual 225%) for all time worked once work starts on a Sunday. 'Weekend daytime hours ... carry no loading' contradicts that for Sunday. Only Saturday daytime seems to carry no loading.

This contradicts the Sunday penalty row at line 1001 (cl 63.4: 200%, casual 225% for all time worked once work starts on a Sunday). Only Saturday daytime seems to carry no loading. The constant is LIVE_PERFORMANCE_AWARD.penaltyNotes[0].
reviewerNotes: I confirm the writer's question. LIVE_PERFORMANCE_AWARD.penaltyNotes[0] says 'weekend daytime hours inside a normal week carry no loading'. The penalty table on the same page (cl 63.4) pays 200% (casual 225%) for all time worked on a Sunday. Only Saturday daytime carries no penalty. The writer did not change this string, which is correct under the no-fact-change rule.

claims: Ordinary hours are worked in a 20-day, 4-week cycle of 8-hour days, with 0.4 of an hour a day accruing towards a rostered day off (cl 15.2).
whys: 20 days of 8 hours is 160 hours, not 152. The hoursNotes entry at line 251 says 19 days of 8 hours plus a paid rostered day off. The two notes on the same page describe the cycle differently. The wording should say the 20-day cycle is 19 working days of 8 hours plus 1 rostered day off. That needs the figure 19, which this pass cannot add.
reviewerNotes: The writer's fact question is valid. PLUMBING_AWARD.penaltyNotes[0] (source line 199) says '20-day, 4-week cycle of 8-hour days', but hoursNotes (source line 251) says 19 days of 8 hours plus a paid rostered day off. A human should reconcile the two against cl 15.2.
